complexity.notes: The debug print inside the loop should be removed (it also adds O(n) I/O overhead), and the math.ceil expressions in it are both unused for the logic and mathematically incorrect for the fleet check (integer ceilings can wrongly equate distinct arrival times) — only the float division comparison is correct. Using sorted(zip(position, speed)) would be more idiomatic than the index-based list comprehension. Starting result at 1 is safe only because the constraints guarantee n >= 1.
complexity.summary: Pairs each car's position and speed, sorts by position, then scans from the car nearest the target backward: a trailing car merges into the lead fleet if its arrival time is no greater than the lead's, otherwise it starts a new fleet and becomes the new lead. Sorting dominates the runtime; the scan is linear.
